items.stem: In a randomized block design with 4 treatments and 6 blocks, the treatment sum of squares is 177, the block sum of squares is 195 and the total sum of squares is 477. The error mean square is
items.explanation: In an RBD, Total SS = Treatment SS + Block SS + Error SS, so Error SS = 477 − 177 − 195 = 105. The error degrees of freedom are (t − 1)(b − 1) = 3 × 5 = 15, so MSE = 105/15 = 7. Trap: dividing by N − t = 20 (the CRD error df) forgets that blocks also use degrees of freedom.

items.stem: A one-way ANOVA compares 4 treatments using 20 observations in all. The treatment sum of squares is 66870 and the error sum of squares is 5344. The calculated F-ratio is
items.explanation: F = (treatment mean square)/(error mean square). Treatment MS = 66870/(4 − 1) = 22290; error MS = 5344/(20 − 4) = 334. F = 11145/167 ≈ 66.7365. Trap: SS_Tr/SS_E = 12.5131 divides sums of squares without their degrees of freedom.

items.stem: N is the incidence matrix of a BIBD with parameters v = 7, b = 7, r = 3, k = 3, λ = 1. The value of |NN′| is
items.explanation: NN′ has r = 3 on the diagonal and λ = 1 everywhere else, i.e. NN′ = (r − λ)I + λJ. Its eigenvalues are r + (v − 1)λ = rk = 9 (once, eigenvector 1) and r − λ = 2 (v − 1 = 6 times). The determinant is their product: |NN′| = rk(r − λ)^(v−1) = 9 × 2^6 = 576. Trap: raising r − λ to the power v counts the eigenvalue rk as if it were r − λ.

items.stem: A 2³ factorial experiment is replicated 2 times, completely randomized (CRD). The error degrees of freedom are
items.explanation: There are 2³ = 8 treatment combinations and N = 16 observations, so total df = 15 and treatment df (all factorial effects) = 7. In a CRD the rest is error: 15 − 7 = 8. Trap: forgetting the block df (or charging block df in a CRD) gives 7.

items.stem: Statements about the principles and layouts of experimental design. Consider the following statements: A. Randomization makes the estimate of experimental error valid. B. Replication provides an estimate of experimental error. C. Local control (blocking) reduces experimental error. D. A completely randomized design uses local control. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: A is true: it guards against systematic bias in the allocation of treatments. B is true: error is measured by the variation between units given the same treatment. C is true: it removes variation between blocks from the error. D is false: a CRD has no blocking. So the answer is A, B, C. Trap: the three principles are randomization, replication and local control; a CRD uses only the first two.

items.stem: Statements about the principles and layouts of experimental design. Consider the following statements: A. A randomized block design uses all three principles. B. A Latin square design controls variation in two directions. C. Increasing replication increases the error variance of a treatment mean. D. In a CRD with t treatments and N units the error degrees of freedom are N − t. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: A is true: it randomizes within blocks, replicates across blocks and blocks for local control. B is true: rows and columns are both blocking factors. C is false: the variance of a mean falls as σ²/r. D is true: N − 1 total minus t − 1 for treatments. So the answer is A, B, D. Trap: the three principles are randomization, replication and local control; a CRD uses only the first two.

items.stem: Statements about the principles and layouts of experimental design. Consider the following statements: A. Randomization removes the need for replication. B. A BIBD is used when a block cannot hold all the treatments. C. In an RBD a block need not contain every treatment. D. Confounding in factorial experiments gives up information on some interactions to reduce block size. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: A is false: without replication there is no estimate of error at all. B is true: blocks are incomplete but balanced. C is false: each block of an RBD is complete. D is true: chosen high-order interactions are mixed with blocks. So the answer is B, D. Trap: the three principles are randomization, replication and local control; a CRD uses only the first two.

items.stem: Statements about the principles and layouts of experimental design. Consider the following statements: A. A Latin square with t treatments needs t² rows. B. A CRD is most suitable when the experimental units are homogeneous. C. Randomization makes the estimate of experimental error valid. D. In an RBD a block need not contain every treatment. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: A is false: it needs t rows and t columns, i.e. t² units. B is true: with no known source of variation there is nothing to block on. C is true: it guards against systematic bias in the allocation of treatments. D is false: each block of an RBD is complete. So the answer is B, C. Trap: the three principles are randomization, replication and local control; a CRD uses only the first two.
